Expectation1: Listen actively and provide emotional support when needed.
Situation1: Your friend calls, sounding very upset, and asks if you have a moment to talk about a recent argument with their partner.
Expectation2: Collaborate with other teams to define and design new features
Situation2: Product has scheduled a general brainstorming session next sprint where attendance is optional
Story: My phone buzzes just as I’m reviewing the invite for next week’s brainstorming session. It’s from Jamie, and I can hear the strain in their voice before they even finish saying hello. “Do you have a minute? I really need to talk,” they say, their words tumbling out in a rush. I know what’s expected of me—I’m the friend who listens, who helps untangle the mess of feelings after a fight. But as Jamie’s voice cracks, my eyes flicker back to my laptop. The brainstorming session is technically optional, but Product made it clear they want input from every team. We’re supposed to come up with ideas for the new feature set, and I know my absence will be noticed. I feel the pressure mounting: Jamie needs me now, but so does my team. My mind races, torn between the urge to be present for my friend and the responsibility to contribute at work. I grip my phone tighter, heart pounding, caught between two worlds that both expect me to show up.
